hero.title: Three years of measurable change in rural Togo.
hero.text: Between 2023 and 2025, APED implemented integrated community development programs across education, maternal health, WASH, vocational training, and women's economic empowerment — achieving a 74% overall implementation rate despite financial and logistical constraints.

figures.label: Vulnerable children supported through education, 256 of them girls

performance.label: Program Performance Summary
performance.title: Sector-by-sector delivery, 2023 – 2025
performance.text: Six program areas, planned vs. achieved. Strong field execution in maternal health and WASH infrastructure; gaps in vocational training and hygiene-kit distribution flag where additional funding will compound impact.

insights.title: Where APED is exceptional
insights.text: Maternal Health (100%) and WASH Infrastructure (100%) demonstrate strong field execution capacity. Women's Economic Empowerment (92%) shows high community engagement and program-fit. These are areas where capital scales directly into outcomes.

insights.title: Where targeted investment compounds
insights.text: Vocational Training (61%) and Hygiene Kits Distribution (70%) underperformed primarily due to resource limitations. Each has a clear unit-cost path to scale — additional funding here removes the bottleneck rather than testing a new theory of change.

challenges.label: Key Challenges
challenges.title: What's standing between APED and 10× impact
items: Limited funding for scaling child health and vaccination programs.
Insufficient resources for expanding vocational training initiatives.
Need for broader WASH awareness and behavior-change campaigns.
Limited access to primary healthcare infrastructure in rural communities.

priority.label: Strategic Priority 2026 – 2028
priority.title: Community Health Center — Kpotamé
paragraphs: Access to healthcare remains a major challenge in Kpotamé and surrounding rural communities. Many households travel long distances to access basic medical consultations, prenatal and postnatal care, child vaccinations, and emergency healthcare.
To address this critical gap, APED has identified the construction of a Community Health Center in Kpotamé as the strategic priority for 2026–2028.

outlook.label: Strategic Outlook 2026 – 2028
